newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria hopes for improved U.S. ties after poll.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria hopes for improved U.S. ties after poll.

text.p: Nigeria's military government said it hoped relations with the United States would be improved after President Bill Clinton's re-election, the government press reported on Thursday.

The Daily Times said military ruler General Sani Abacha said in a message to Clinton that his re-election "is a clear demonstration of the recognition by Americans of your commitment to their national aspirations".
Abacha expressed Nigeria's firm belief that relations between the two countries would grow stronger over the next four years, it said.

Relations between Nigeria and the United States, which buys 40 percent of the crude oil produced by the African nation, have been strained since 1993 when the then military president annulled a presidential election to restore democracy.

The U.S. and other Western powers further slammed sanctions on Nigeria last year when the country defied worldwide pleas for clemency and hanged nine minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa for murder.
